conditions.label: Ruptured corpus luteum cyst with hemoperitoneum

reports.text: Transabdominal pelvic ultrasound, transvaginal views deferred for pain. Uterus normal in size and contour. Endometrium thin. Ovaries not well seen. Free fluid in the cul-de-sac.
Specimen: right ovarian cyst wall, excision. Cyst lined by luteinized granulosa and theca cells with fresh hemorrhage and organizing blood clot.
reports.conclusion: Hemorrhagic corpus luteum cyst, right ovary. No malignancy.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Outside ED / GYN record, 02/20/2023.

31-year-old woman with HTN, Rh negative, and a ruptured hepatocellular adenoma resected in Feb 2022. Came in about 4 hours after the start of sharp, constant lower abdominal pain that came on after a hard workout, with some crampy waves on top. Nauseated, no vomiting. LMP 2 weeks ago, normal flow.

Meds: HCTZ 25 daily. (Outside med list also shows combined OCP.) Allergy: PCN - hives.

Triage: BP 90/60, HR 120, RR 22, T 37.2.
Exam: abdomen diffusely tender, rigid, rebound present. Pelvic deferred due to pain.
Labs: Hgb 11.2 (13.5 last fall per PCP), WBC 12.0. Urine hCG negative.
US: free fluid in the cul-de-sac.

Course: IV fluid boluses. Despite this HR climbed and BP fell to 85/55. GYN at bedside, consented for diagnostic laparoscopy, to OR emergently.

documents.title: Operative Report - Laparoscopy
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
Date: 02/20/2023
Preop: hemoperitoneum, suspected ruptured ovarian cyst. Postop: ruptured right corpus luteum cyst with hemoperitoneum.
Procedure: laparoscopy, evacuation of hemoperitoneum, right ovarian cystectomy.
Findings: hemoperitoneum with clot in the pelvis. Right ovary with a ruptured hemorrhagic cyst, oozing at the rupture site. Left ovary and both tubes normal. Uterus with expected appearance after prior cesareans. Upper abdomen: liver resection site well healed.
Cyst wall excised, ovarian bed hemostatic with bipolar. Hemoperitoneum evacuated and pelvis irrigated.
No transfusion. No complications.

documents.title: Discharge Summary
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
Admit 02/20/2023 - discharge 02/22/2023.
Dx: ruptured right corpus luteum cyst with hemoperitoneum, s/p laparoscopic evacuation and right ovarian cystectomy. Acute blood loss.

Uncomplicated recovery. Tolerating diet, ambulating, pain controlled with acetaminophen. Hgb 10.2 on day of discharge. Pathology pending at discharge.

Plan: ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily x 3 months. Continue home HCTZ. Light activity 2 weeks. GYN post-op visit 2-3 weeks. PCP 1 week for CBC.
Allergies: penicillin (hives).

documents.title: Pt update - hospitalized
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt called from hospital. Had emergency laparoscopy last night for a bleeding ovarian cyst. Feeling better today, expects discharge tomorrow. Booked PCP post-hospital visit 3/1. Records requested.

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here after admission 2/20-2/22: sudden lower abd pain after a hard workout, hemoperitoneum, hypotensive despite fluids, laparoscopy found a ruptured R corpus luteum cyst. Cystectomy, no transfusion. D/c Hgb 10.2. Path: hemorrhagic corpus luteum cyst, benign.

Feels ok. Port sites a bit sore. Taking iron. No fever, no bleeding.
Meds: HCTZ 25 daily, ferrous sulfate 325 daily.
Note: hospital med list still shows the combined OCP - she has not taken it since Feb 2022. Asked her to tell OB to update their list.

Exam: well, BP fine. Abd soft, 3 small port incisions clean and healing.

A/P
- Ruptured R corpus luteum cyst w/ hemoperitoneum, s/p lap. Recovering. GYN post-op visit 3/14.
- Blood loss anemia: CBC today, iron x 3 mo then recheck.
- Two big intra-abdominal bleeds in a year (liver 2022, ovary now), different causes, both with clear structural sources. No bruising, heavy periods or bleeding with past surgeries/deliveries. INR normal last year. Not pursuing a bleeding workup now; low threshold if anything else.
- HTN controlled.

documents.title: Gynecology Post-op Letter
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
Dear Colleague,

Your patient was seen 03/14/2023 two weeks after laparoscopic evacuation of hemoperitoneum and right ovarian cystectomy for a ruptured corpus luteum cyst. Final pathology confirmed a hemorrhagic corpus luteum cyst with no malignancy. Incisions are healed and she is comfortable.

Corpus luteum rupture usually does not recur, though it can. She is not on hormonal contraception given her hepatic adenoma history, and estrogen should stay off the table. We talked through progestin-only options which would also help with cycle irregularity; she is not interested at present.

She may resume all activity. Return as needed.

Medications: hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily; ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily.
Allergies: penicillin (hives).

documents.body:
BP f/u. Feeling well since the laparoscopy, back to the gym. Work busy.
Meds: HCTZ 25 mg daily, taking reliably. Off iron.
BP slightly higher than usual today, repeat similar. Heart regular, lungs clear, no edema.
A/P: HTN, acceptable. Continue HCTZ, BMP. Asked her to check a few home readings before the fall physical. Cuff size reviewed.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
32F annual.

Since last year: ruptured R corpus luteum cyst Feb 2023 with laparoscopic cystectomy; recovered, Hgb normal by May. Hepatic adenoma resected 2022, no further imaging needed.
Home BPs 118-128/76-82 per her log.
Cycles irregular, 5-8 wks. Not on hormonal contraception (no estrogen given adenoma); declines progestin options again, aware they are available.

Meds: HCTZ 25 daily. Allergy PCN.
SH: HR, partnered, never smoker, drinks rarely, exercising 3-4x/wk. PHQ-2 0.

Exam: well. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abd soft, well-healed scars, no masses, nontender. Ext no edema. Skin nl.

Plan: CBC, CMP. Flu today. Updated covid shot in a few weeks when it's in. Co-test due 2025. Lipids/A1c next year.

reports.text: Portable AP chest. Lungs clear. No pneumothorax or pleural effusion. Mediastinum not widened. Heart size normal. No displaced rib fracture.

documents.title: Trauma ED Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Outside ED record, DOS 02/21/2024.

32F, restrained driver in a head-on collision at moderate speed, airbags deployed. No LOC. Complains of dizziness, fatigue and mild belly pain; denies other injury. Hx resected liver adenoma 2022, ruptured ovarian cyst 2023, HTN on HCTZ, O neg. PCN allergy (hives).

Primary survey intact. VS: BP 90/60, HR 120, RR 22, SpO2 97% RA.
Secondary: alert, pale and anxious. Skin cool and clammy. Abd: mild LUQ tenderness, no rebound or guarding, BS normal. Pelvic and rectal unremarkable. No seat-belt sign, no external trauma.

Labs: Hgb 9.8, Hct 29, plt 250, PT 12, PTT 30, lactate 4.2.
FAST: negative for free fluid. CXR: normal.

Assessment: hypovolemic shock after MVC.
ED course: crystalloid bolus, then 2 units O-negative PRBC with HR down to the 90s and BP 112/70. Admitted to trauma service for overnight observation with serial exams and Hgb.

documents.title: Trauma Observation Discharge
documents.author: trauma surgery
documents.body:
Admitted 02/21/2024 for observation after MVC with hypovolemic shock, responded to 2 units PRBC. Serial abdominal exams remained benign overnight. Hgb 10.4 this morning, stable. Tolerating diet, ambulating, vitals normal.

Discharged 02/22/2024. Resume HCTZ 25 mg daily when eating and drinking normally. Return for worsening abdominal pain, lightheadedness, fainting. PCP follow-up within 1 week with CBC.
Allergies: penicillin.

documents.title: Post-ED call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt called. Car accident Wed, needed 2 units of blood in the ED, kept overnight, home yesterday. A little woozy when she stands fast. No new belly pain, no fainting. Drinking well. Advised slow position changes, ED if fainting or worse pain. Appt 2/28 with PCP.

events.reason: Follow-up after car accident and transfusion

documents.title: Post-ED Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
One week after head-on MVC. ED: BP 90/60, HR 120, Hgb 9.8, lactate 4.2, FAST neg, CXR neg; given 2 u PRBC with good response, observed overnight, Hgb 10.4 at d/c.

Now: lightheadedness gone. Tired. Abd pain resolved. Back at work from home this week.
Meds: HCTZ 25 (restarted 2/23).

Exam: NAD. BP ok, HR normal. Abd soft, nontender, no LUQ tenderness, no masses. No bruising.

A/P
- Hypovolemic shock after MVC, s/p transfusion. Stable and well. CBC today; start ferrous sulfate 325 daily, recheck CBC + ferritin in 8 wks.
- O neg, received O neg units; antibody screen at next pregnancy per routine.
- HTN, continue HCTZ.
Paperwork for her auto insurer will go through records.

documents.title: Records request
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Auto insurance adjuster requested records related to 2/21 MVC. Signed authorization from patient on file (scanned). Sent 2/28 office note and ED/discharge records per authorization.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
33F, annual.

Interval: MVC Feb 2024 with hypovolemic shock, 2 u PRBC, observed overnight; Hgb back to 12.9 by April. No lasting injury.
HTN: home BPs mid 120s/high 70s.
Gyn: cycles still irregular. No contraception currently; she and her partner are open to another pregnancy. Reviewed that she should let us and OB know early if she becomes pregnant - Rh negative, prior classical cesarean, HTN on HCTZ, adenoma history. Advised a prenatal vitamin with folic acid while not preventing pregnancy.

Meds: HCTZ 25 daily. Allergy PCN (hives).
SH unchanged. Never smoker, rare alcohol. PHQ-2 1 (a few stressful weeks at work).

Exam: well-appearing. HEENT nl. Thyroid nl. CV RRR. Lungs CTA. Abd soft, healed scars, NT. No edema. Skin nl.

Plan: CBC, CMP, lipids, A1c. Flu and updated covid today. Co-test due next year.

documents.title: Physical labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Taylor, labs from Tuesday all look fine. Blood count normal, potassium and kidney function normal on the HCTZ, liver tests normal, LDL 105, which flags just over the lab's cutoff but is fine for you, A1c normal.
